_note: Biblical places and where they are now. Every entry carries a `certainty` field, because the difference between an excavated site and a pious tradition matters and most apps blur it.

_certainty.continuous: The city never stopped being inhabited — the modern city IS the ancient one.
_certainty.traditional: A long-held identification, plausible but not proven.
_certainty.disputed: Scholars propose several sites. No consensus.

places.name: Garden of Eden
places.note: No location is known. Proposals have placed it in Armenia, near the Caspian, in Syria, in southern Arabia and in Babylonia. Easton's own entry from 1897 calls it the most discussed geographical question there is. Anyone who tells you where it was is guessing.

places.name: Ararat
places.note: Genesis says the ark rested on 'the mountains of Ararat' — a region, not a peak. The identification with this specific mountain is later tradition.

places.name: Babel / Babylon
places.note: Extensively excavated, about 85 km south of Baghdad. The tower is usually connected with Etemenanki, the great ziggurat whose foundations survive.

places.name: Ur of the Chaldees
places.note: Abraham's birthplace. The ziggurat still stands, one of the best preserved in Mesopotamia.

places.name: Nineveh
places.note: The mounds of Kuyunjik and Nebi Yunus sit inside modern Mosul. Jonah's city; much of the site was destroyed in 2014-2015.

places.name: Sodom and Gomorrah
places.note: Bab edh-Dhra and Numeira are the long-standing candidates; Tall el-Hammam north of the Dead Sea has been argued more recently. Nothing is settled.

places.name: Mount Sinai / Horeb
places.note: The traditional site has St Catherine's Monastery at its foot and dates to Byzantine times. Jebel al-Lawz in Saudi Arabia and several Negev peaks have also been proposed.

places.name: Jericho
places.note: Among the oldest continuously occupied places on earth, with walls dating back roughly 10,000 years.

places.name: Jerusalem
places.note: Never ceased to be inhabited. The City of David, the Temple Mount and the Pool of Siloam are all visitable.

places.name: Bethlehem
places.note: About 10 km south of Jerusalem. The Church of the Nativity has stood over the traditional site since the 4th century.

places.name: Nazareth
places.note: A small village of perhaps a few hundred people in the first century; now the largest Arab city in Israel.

places.name: Capernaum
places.note: Jesus' base in Galilee. The synagogue ruins and the house traditionally held to be Peter's are both excavated.

places.name: Sea of Galilee
places.note: Also called Gennesaret and Tiberias in scripture. Israel's largest freshwater lake.

places.name: Mount Carmel
places.note: Where Elijah confronted the prophets of Baal.

places.name: Mount Nebo
places.note: Where Moses saw the promised land. On a clear day you can see Jericho and the hills of Jerusalem.

places.name: Hebron
places.note: The Cave of Machpelah, burial place of Abraham and Sarah, lies under a Herodian enclosure still standing.

places.name: Shiloh
places.note: Where the tabernacle stood before the temple, and where Samuel was called.

places.name: Megiddo
places.note: A UNESCO site with 26 layers of settlement. The name behind 'Armageddon' — Har Megiddo, the hill of Megiddo.

places.name: Damascus
places.note: Among the oldest continuously inhabited cities anywhere. Straight Street, where Paul lodged after his conversion, is still a street.

places.name: Antioch
places.note: Where believers were first called Christians. Severely damaged in the 2023 earthquake.

places.name: Tarsus
places.note: Paul's birthplace.

places.name: Ephesus
places.note: One of the best-preserved classical cities in the Mediterranean. The theatre where the silversmiths rioted still stands.

places.name: Smyrna
places.note: Second of the seven churches. Now Türkiye's third largest city.

places.name: Pergamum
places.note: The acropolis and its steep theatre survive above the modern town.

places.name: Thyatira
places.note: Lydia, the seller of purple, came from here. Remains sit within the modern town.

places.name: Sardis
places.note: Once capital of Lydia and fabulously rich. The synagogue and gymnasium are excavated.

places.name: Philadelphia
places.note: The church that was told it had 'a little strength'. Still a working town.

places.name: Laodicea
places.note: The lukewarm church. Its water arrived by aqueduct from hot springs at Hierapolis and cold springs elsewhere — tepid by the time it came, which is likely the point of the rebuke.

places.name: Colossae
places.note: Located but barely excavated — the mound is still largely untouched.

places.name: Troas
places.note: Where Paul saw the vision of the man of Macedonia, and where Eutychus fell from the window.

places.name: Miletus
places.note: Where Paul said farewell to the Ephesian elders. Silt has left the once-great harbour several kilometres inland.

places.name: Athens
places.note: The Areopagus, where Paul spoke of the unknown god, is a bare rock below the Acropolis that you can still climb.

places.name: Corinth
places.note: The bema — the judgment seat where Paul stood before Gallio — is excavated and identifiable.

places.name: Philippi
places.note: A UNESCO site. The traditional place of Lydia's baptism is on the river nearby.

places.name: Berea
places.note: Whose people 'searched the scriptures daily'.

places.name: Patmos
places.note: Where John received the Revelation. The Cave of the Apocalypse is a pilgrimage site.

places.name: Malta
places.note: Where Paul was shipwrecked. St Paul's Bay is the traditional landing place.

places.name: Tyre
places.note: Alexander's siege causeway permanently joined the island city to the mainland; it is a peninsula now.

places.name: Joppa
places.note: Where Jonah took ship, and where Peter saw the sheet let down from heaven.

places.name: Caesarea Maritima
places.note: Herod's harbour city. The theatre, hippodrome and aqueduct are excavated; part of the harbour is now underwater.

places.name: Caesarea Philippi
places.note: Where Peter confessed Jesus as the Christ, before a cliff face full of pagan shrines.

places.name: Bethel
places.note: Where Jacob dreamed of the ladder. The identification with Beitin is widely held but not certain.

places.name: Bethany
places.note: Home of Mary, Martha and Lazarus. The Arabic name means 'place of Lazarus'.

places.name: Cana
places.note: Kafr Kanna is the pilgrimage site, but Khirbet Qana some 9 km north is the stronger archaeological candidate.

places.name: Mount Hermon
places.note: Often proposed as the mount of the Transfiguration, though Tabor holds the older tradition.

places.name: Shushan / Susa
places.note: Esther's city, and where Daniel saw the vision of the ram and goat. A UNESCO site.

places.name: No-Amon / Thebes
places.note: The Egyptian capital denounced by Nahum and Jeremiah. Karnak and the Valley of the Kings are here.

places.name: Alexandria
places.note: Apollos came from here, and it is where the Septuagint was made.

places.name: Mount Ebal and Mount Gerizim
places.note: The mountains of blessing and cursing, facing each other across the valley where Nablus now sits. Shechem lay between them.

places.name: Emmaus
places.note: Four candidate sites, none agreed. Luke's stated distance from Jerusalem varies between manuscripts, which is part of the difficulty.
